insights.insight: Static source can expose a plausible state path without establishing that the integrated product actually exhibits the defect; route to the cheapest integrated discriminator before granting build permission.
insights.promotion_reason: Already encoded by discrimination-before-redesign and reality-floor rules. OSS-0007 is a useful neighbor: a directly visible guard-contract asymmetry can justify a narrow reversible build at R1 without waiting for field evidence. OSS-0013 and OSS-0029 exercise the same boundary in HOLDOUT and remain score-only until the wave closes.

insights.insight: Independent evidence about a neighboring bug or the same component can support a failure family without confirming the exact mechanism under adjudication.
insights.promotion_reason: Recurring adjudication hazard, but still lacks an executable positive-control gate and closed holdout wave. BATCH-007 added Butterfly and Linkwarden examples. BATCH-008 added an adversarial same-component example: Twenty's historical ConfirmationModal Enter-key bug was not allowed to confirm a distinct async-delete failure mechanism. BATCH-011 added a tighter TRAIN example: Docmost PR #2302 confirms a stale-state defect in the same move-page flow, but it does not confirm the frozen pre-selection enabled-no-op mechanism. BATCH-016 adds Pomatez: several Strict Mode anti-circumvention reports support the policy family but do not confirm that the unguarded Sessions refresh control bypasses the active strict timer.

insights.insight: A suspicious timing workaround is not itself permission to refactor; first reproduce the event mechanism with and without the workaround.
insights.promotion_reason: Single case, no neighbor control, no positive control and no HOLDOUT evidence.

insights.insight: A repository can establish exactly what the product does while remaining unable to establish that the behavior is a defect; when the unresolved question is intended interaction/configuration policy, route to OWNER instead of converting implementation certainty into build permission.
insights.promotion_reason: Already encoded by Neta's evidence/authority/permission separation. BATCH-009 adds two materially different TRAIN replications: TaskCoach's documented Flatpak compatibility tradeoff and DooTask's mixed-scheme self-hosting topology both show that an implementation fact can be certain while the change decision remains OWNER-owned. BATCH-013 adds SiYuan as an ADVERSARIAL explicit-intent replication: a named no-confirm deletion option was intentionally requested by a maintainer, so generic safety concerns cannot convert known behavior into a defect without OWNER permission. OSS-0040 is compatible with this family but remains unresolved and is therefore retained as case memory rather than counted as a replication.

insights.insight: When a product contract is explicit and equivalent controls already enforce it, one unguarded sibling path can justify a narrow reversible consistency fix without asserting any field outcome.
insights.promotion_reason: OSS-0014 exposes the missing boundary in this family: sibling equivalence is not itself an explicit product contract. Actual Budget's confirmation-versus-undo tradeoff was OWNER-owned, so asymmetry alone could not grant BUILD permission. OSS-0026 is a HOLDOUT score-only case in which an explicit local error/empty-state contract supported a narrow build; it is not used to promote the family before wave close.

insights.insight: Source can prove that a warning, recovery gesture, or affordance exists; it cannot prove that people notice, understand, or successfully use it. Adequacy claims about discoverability or error prevention require FIELD evidence rather than additional UI by default.
insights.promotion_reason: This is a concrete transfer instance of the existing R6/field-outcome rule, not a new heuristic. OSS-0010 independently exercises the same boundary in HOLDOUT and is score-only until the wave closes.

insights.insight: Equivalent-looking sibling paths do not establish a shared product contract. Before turning asymmetry into BUILD permission, distinguish an explicit invariant from a consistency preference or interaction-policy tradeoff that belongs to OWNER.
insights.promotion_reason: OSS-0018 showed that similar controls can legitimately apply different guards when consequences differ. OSS-0030 adds an adversarial lifecycle example: an inline TODO plus a sibling option did not authorize work in a legacy codebase whose owner is rewriting the product. OSS-0034 adds a TRAIN mobile deletion-policy replication: Organic Maps maintainer discussion explicitly treats confirmation as context-dependent across bookmarks, tracks and lists, so a sibling asymmetry still does not establish one shared contract. The candidate still lacks an executable discrimination gate, deliberate red positive control and unseen HOLDOUT success, so it remains memory only.

insights.insight: Static source can show a recovery promise and recovery machinery but cannot establish the operational guarantee that support or a deployed environment can actually deliver. Calibrate such promises from an ENVIRONMENT/support drill rather than from UI reachability alone.
insights.promotion_reason: A concrete transfer instance of the canonical reality/authority separation. OSS-0028 is a HOLDOUT score-only case where following a delegated startup path found the promised local guard; it is not used as learning evidence before wave close.

insights.insight: A database transaction does not make external filesystem, search-index, network, or other side effects atomic. When a decision depends on rollback consistency across authorities, explicitly identify the external side-effect boundary and leave a failure-injection gate before treating the repair as proven.
insights.promotion_reason: The static code clearly exposes a cross-boundary atomicity risk, but post-freeze issue evidence did not reproduce the exact rollback inconsistency. Keep as technical case memory until a deliberate failure-injection fixture can turn red and a neighboring safe transaction boundary is available as control. OSS-0044 exercises this boundary in HOLDOUT and remains score-only; it is not counted as a replication or promotion input before wave close.
